title: Eyes First
focusTag: Reading the Ball off the Wall
intro: On court you don't choose when to move. The ball chooses for you. Every drill here ends with you reacting to a ball you can't fully predict. It's the lightest of the four on your legs, thirty-four reactions, most of them in sets of four throws.

You need a wall you're allowed to hit a ball against, and a ball. Without a wall, skip this one today. For the last block, start about six metres from the wall. Do it early in the day on fresh legs, before hitting or conditioning, because tired legs make you read late. Keep it 48 hours away from hard running or jumping. The day before a match is fine, but skip the Back Away block then. Don't do it on match day. If you start reacting late or missing more, end the session there.

before.label: Not today
before.text: A sore ankle, knee, calf, hamstring, groin or Achilles, or an injury in the last month? Get it looked at first.

before.label: Stop and get it checked
before.text: A sharp pain, pain that spreads, numbness, swelling, a joint that gives way, or a sudden pull or pop.

before.label: Stop now
before.text: Chest pain, dizziness, a heartbeat that races or skips, or breathing that doesn't feel right. Get it looked at before you train again. Told to be careful with hard exercise? Check with your doctor first.

before.label: Check the space
before.text: About eight metres of clear floor behind you to back into, and nothing you could trip on. Keep other balls in a bag or your pockets, because stepping on a loose ball is an easy way to roll an ankle.

good: Jog easy until you're warm and breathing a little harder
Feel your legs loosen up with every minute
Hold a wall and swing the leg front to back, then side to side
Feel the hip loosen up as the swing gets bigger
bad: Arching your lower back to throw the leg higher

good: Step wide and sit back into that hip, chest tall
Feel the inside of the straight leg stretch
bad: Letting the bent knee cave inward

good: Shuffle ten metres each length, staying low and pushing the floor away with the trailing foot
Feel your thighs and glutes working to keep you low
bad: Bobbing up and down between steps

good: Cross the back foot in front, then behind, as you travel sideways
Feel the twist through your hips as you cross over
bad: Twisting your shoulders along with your hips

good: Take a small hop and land wide and low on the balls of both feet
Landing loaded and ready to push either way
Add speed on each run, about 60, then 80, then 90 percent of your top speed
Fast but relaxed, never straining
bad: Going flat out on the first one

good: Throw hard at the wall, split-step as it hits, then move to where it comes off
Your feet already set when the ball reaches you
bad: Chasing the ball without checking how close the wall is

good: Bounce the ball hard off the floor at an angle, then chase it down before the second bounce
Your eyes reading the bounce before your feet move
bad: Stepping on the ball as you chase it

exercises.name: Backpedal and Turn
exercises.note: Alternate sides. Do the first two at half speed to get the feel, then build up.

good: Face the wall and throw the ball hard into it, backpedal away while you watch the rebound, then turn and chase it down
Your hips turning as you read where the ball is going
bad: Backpedalling faster than you can control
